chapters.title: Modeling decisions and the geometry of linear programming
objectives: Translate resource, coverage, and balance requirements into a linear model
Distinguish affine geometry, convexity, feasibility, and optimality
Derive the connection between vertices and basic feasible solutions
Check a small linear program by enumeration and an independent solver
chapters.prerequisites: Vectors, matrix multiplication, elementary linear algebra; convexity is developed here.

chapters.title: Simplex, artificial variables, and exceptional cases
objectives: Derive reduced costs and the primal ratio test from a basis
Trace a complete simplex solve and construct an unbounded ray
Separate feasibility from profit using a two-phase auxiliary problem
Diagnose degeneracy, cycling, and alternate optima
chapters.prerequisites: Chapter 1: LP models, rank, vertices, and basic feasible solutions.

chapters.title: Dual certificates, dual simplex, and sensitivity
objectives: Construct a dual from bound arguments and sign restrictions
Use weak duality and complementary slackness to certify an optimum
Derive and trace a dual-simplex pivot
Calculate valid ranges for changes in capacities, profits, columns, and constraints
chapters.prerequisites: Chapters 1–2: equality-form bases, reduced costs, and primal simplex.

chapters.title: Integer programming: valid cuts and complete search
objectives: Use an LP relaxation as an objective bound without treating its solution as integer feasible
Derive a Gomory fractional cut and a mixed-integer split cut
Trace branch-and-bound with valid incumbent pruning
Recognize modeling and numerical conditions needed for an integer optimum certificate
chapters.prerequisites: Chapters 1–3: LP relaxation geometry, basis dictionaries, reduced costs, and dual simplex.

chapters.title: Transportation, network bases, and assignment
objectives: Formulate balanced shipping and interpret dummy supplies or demands
Construct an initial transportation basis and improve it with cycle pivots
Use row and column potentials as optimality certificates
Explain why integer balances admit integer transportation and assignment optima
Trace the Hungarian reduced-cost adjustment
chapters.prerequisites: Chapters 1–4: LP geometry, bases, reduced costs, dual certificates, and integer restrictions.

chapters.title: Project networks, critical paths, and uncertain deadlines
objectives: Translate precedence statements into a valid project network
Derive earliest and latest event times and distinguish activity floats
Use PERT estimates without confusing a path approximation with a project guarantee
Analyze how crashing changes the set of binding paths
chapters.prerequisites: Directed graphs, elementary probability, and the LP modeling conventions of chapters 1–3.

chapters.title: Shortest paths and tours: local certificates and global connectivity
objectives: Derive relaxation and Dijkstra's label-setting invariant
Distinguish a shortest path tree from an all-pairs solution
Formulate TSP with subtour elimination and interpret assignment bounds
Prove the doubled-tree metric approximation and identify its assumptions
chapters.prerequisites: Directed graphs and DAG recurrences from chapter 6; assignment models from chapter 5.

chapters.title: Stationary points, curvature, and global optimality
objectives: Derive first- and second-order local optimality conditions
Classify degenerate stationary points without overusing the Hessian test
Distinguish positive definiteness from semidefiniteness and test them correctly
Prove convexity-based global optimality and separate uniqueness from existence
chapters.prerequisites: Multivariable differentiation, Taylor expansion, and symmetric-matrix eigenvalues.

chapters.title: Equality constraints, KKT conditions, and sensitivity
objectives: Derive Lagrange stationarity from feasible tangent directions
Use reduced curvature instead of demanding a positive-definite bordered matrix
Apply all four KKT conditions with consistent multiplier signs
Separate constraint qualification, convex sufficiency, and sensitivity assumptions
chapters.prerequisites: Local and global optimality, gradients, Hessians, convexity, and LP duality.

chapters.title: Interval elimination, Fibonacci search, and golden sections
objectives: Prove interval elimination under explicit unimodality and tie assumptions
Separate bracketing, location tolerance, objective error, and evaluation budgets
Derive dichotomous and interval-halving contraction laws
Derive Fibonacci sample reuse and the golden-section fixed point
chapters.prerequisites: Scalar functions, inequalities, finite sequences, and the distinction between local and global minima.

chapters.title: Interpolation, direct search, and gradient descent
objectives: Construct quadratic and cubic local models
Trace a nonlinear simplex update
Derive exact line search for a positive definite quadratic
Diagnose misleading stopping tests and finite differences
chapters.prerequisites: One-variable minimization, gradients, Hessians, positive definite matrices, and Chapter 10 bracketing.

chapters.title: Feasible directions, cutting planes, and penalty paths
objectives: Distinguish linearized feasibility from feasible motion
Build globally valid convex cutting planes
Derive exterior-penalty and interior-barrier limits
Use primal and dual residuals to stop constrained optimization
chapters.prerequisites: Gradients, convexity, LP duality, KKT conditions, and Chapter 11 line search.

chapters.title: Separable programming and controlled linear approximations
objectives: Recognize additive separability and its coordinate dependence
Build adjacent-weight piecewise linear models
Distinguish an interpolation graph from its convex hull
Bound approximation error and recheck nonlinear feasibility
chapters.prerequisites: Linear programming, convex combinations, one-variable interpolation, and convexity.

chapters.title: Geometric programming: positive models and dual certificates
objectives: Recognize monomials and posynomials on a positive domain
Derive the logarithmic convex transformation
Construct arithmetic–geometric mean dual bounds
Distinguish ordinary GP from reversed-posynomial generalizations
chapters.prerequisites: Logarithms, convexity, Lagrange multipliers, and weak duality.

chapters.title: Dynamic programming: state, recursion, and resource allocation
objectives: Define a sufficient state and a Bellman recursion
Solve and reconstruct an integer resource allocation
Derive continuous additive and multiplicative recursions
Separate uncertain inputs from sequential information arrival
chapters.prerequisites: Integer programming, elementary probability, single-variable calculus, and shortest paths.

chapters.title: Multiple objectives, AHP, and TOPSIS
objectives: Separate dominance from preference
Choose among scalarization, goals, lexicographic and epsilon constraints
Derive consistent AHP priorities and diagnose inconsistency
Implement TOPSIS with explicit directions, normalization and sensitivity
chapters.prerequisites: Vector inequalities, convexity, eigenvectors, linear programming, and Euclidean distance.
